thread_dispositions.reply_body: Appearance saves now refuse a non-object terminalFont value with a diagnostic and roll back the tentative selection. The original file stays byte-for-byte intact. The keymap regression covers null, a number, an array and a string; keymap and scoped static analysis pass.

The guard deliberately treats a disconnected or replaced view as an unknown process lifetime. A service-owned agent can still be running after its view disconnects; clearing live_ or allowing ordinary removal would discard that identity. The existing Close action provides the explicit abandon path for an unreachable agent, and Commands offers Reconnect. No removal-policy change is needed.

Duplicate of the disconnected-view removal finding. Transport loss is not proof of process exit. removeSession preserves that distinction; closeSession(id, true) is the explicit unreachable-agent abandonment path. Retaining this safeguard.

Registry loading must preserve the original launch fingerprint even when an executable or directory has disappeared: the service may still be alive and reconnectable. Rejecting that row in loadAgents would reject the whole saved workspace and prevent recovery. This PR reconnects saved services; restart validation belongs at launch time, and the stacked continuity PR validates the executable/directory in restoredLaunch. Retaining structural validation during registry loading.

Duplicate of the missing-executable restore finding. Reconnecting an existing service does not launch the saved program, and dropping or rejecting its registry row would lose the recovery path. Launch-time validation is handled by restoredLaunch in the stacked continuity work; loadAgents intentionally preserves saved identity.

terminate() returning false means no termination request was sent (the view is not input-ready or its transport rejected the write). There is no pending close for finishClosing to finish. The current error already says to reconnect or exit the agent. Setting closing=true in this branch would falsely mark an unsent request as pending; a successfully sent request still sets closing and enables the legacy-service reconnect path.

Duplicate of the failed-terminate finding. finishClosing handles a sent close request, including rejection by an older service; terminate()==false leaves no request to reconcile. The existing diagnostic explicitly offers reconnect/exit, so keeping closing=false is intentional.

The harness snapshots both configuration and registry state during prepare and restores them after stopping its writers, including deleting files that were originally absent. Repeated cleanup is idempotent. A background regression exercises two consecutive runs for both a fresh runtime and --keep.

Covered by the same QA cleanup repair: original registry/configuration bytes are restored, originally absent files are removed, and a second cleanup cannot delete the restored files. The repeated-run regression passes for fresh and --keep fixtures.
